title: Alert noise reduction — manager brief & all-hands talking points
body:
Purpose:
This is a short, manager-facing brief plus a 90s all-hands script for the alert-noise-reduction initiative we're starting this month. Goal: reduce actionable alert noise by ~40% over the next quarter without increasing time-to-detect real incidents. Use this for team leads, oncall handoffs, and the all-hands segment.

TL;DR (for managers):
- What's happening: We're tuning thresholds, consolidating duplicate alerts, and introducing a suppression window for known-flaky signals (deployment-related spikes).
- Why: Too many low-signal alerts are increasing cognitive load and delaying real incident response. Early experiments show ~28% fewer paging events with no detection loss.
- What managers should do: 1) Read the updated runbook and opt-in team pilot by Mon 02/24; 2) Share the 90s script in your next team standup; 3) Ensure your oncall has the updated playbook and has run the simulation.

What changed (engineer summary, keep it short):
- Threshold tuning: memory and tail-latency alerts raised to 95th/99th percentiles with adaptive cooldowns.
- Consolidation: similar alerts from inference runtime + autoscaler now mapped to single composite alert with runbook mapping.
- Flaky-signal suppression: transient alerts during rolling deploy windows are suppressed for 10m by default and surfaced as digest entries rather than pages.
- Rapid rollback policy: critical production regressions still page immediately via a separate high-severity channel.

Manager talking points (use these verbatim in syncs):
- "We’re rolling out changes to reduce noisy pages so engineers can focus on real incidents and ship faster."
- "This is conservative: anything classified as critical still pages immediately; these changes target low-signal/duplicate churn."
- "We’re running a pilot this quarter and will measure page counts, MTTR, and missed-detection risk before wider rollout."
- "If your team relies on any custom alerting thresholds, please add those to the pilot tracker by EOD Friday so we can account for them."

All-hands 90s script (CEO or Head of SRE):
- 0–20s: One-liner context: "We’ve heard from many teams that alert noise is causing real disruption to product work — we’re fixing that."
- 20–60s: What we’re doing: "Small, safe changes: consolidating duplicates, tuning thresholds, suppressing deploy noise, and keeping a hard line on critical pages."
- 60–80s: Reassurance: "We’ll validate with metrics (pages/day, MTTR) and run a pilot before full rollout."
- 80–90s: Call to action: "Managers — make sure oncall simulations run this week and add any team-specific constraints to the tracker."

Anticipated Q&A (short answers):
- Q: "Will important alerts be suppressed?"
  A: "No — severity mapping unchanged. Suppression targets low-signal events only; critical channels remain untouched."
- Q: "How do we opt teams into the pilot?"
  A: "Add your team in the Linear epic (linked) and run the short simulation checklist in the runbook."
- Q: "How will we measure success?"
  A: "Primary metrics: pages/day (target -40%), MTTR (no degradation), and handoff/ack latency."
- Q: "What if my product needs a lower threshold?"
  A: "Flag it in the tracker and we’ll add team-specific exceptions or a separate alert route."

Slack short-template for #platform-ops (for managers to post):
- "Heads up: starting this week we’re piloting alert noise reduction (consolidation + suppression). Critical pages unchanged. Please ensure your oncall completes the simulation and add exceptions to the tracker: <Linear link>. Reach out to @Inez for questions."

Immediate action items (for this week):
- Managers: confirm team opt-in or exception list by Mon 02/24.
- Oncall engineers: complete 15m simulation from the runbook and post results in the pilot thread.
- SRE leads: monitor the pilot dashboard and share a preliminary snapshot at next week’s tactical.

Follow-ups and timeline:
- Week 1 (pilot kickoff): run simulations, finalize exception list.
- Week 2–4 (pilot run): collect pages/day, MTTR; run one canary change.
- End of month: present pilot results and recommended rollouts.

Notes for managers (short checklist):
- Ensure oncall has run the simulation.
- Confirm any team exceptions in the tracker.
- Read the updated runbook and paste the Slack template in your team channel.

Runbook & simulation links (quick):
- Runbook: ops-runbooks/alerting-v2.md (PR linked above).
- Simulation checklist: 15m oncall shakeout -> validate alerts route to composite channel -> confirm non-critical events arrive as digest.

Open questions (for SRE leads):
- Should suppression windows be adaptive (based on deploy length) rather than flat 10m?
- Do we need a separate digest cadence for teams that want hourly vs daily summaries?

Notes to self: keep manager comms short and repeatable; avoid technical deep dives in the all-hands. This doc is the canonical manager cheat-sheet for week 1.

— Devon
